images.title: More than, less than or equal to one
images.purpose: Show 8/5, 3/10 and 10/10 as shaded pieces against one whole of the same length, so the child sees that 8 pieces of 1/5 pass one whole, 3 pieces of 1/10 fall short and 10 pieces of 1/10 fill it exactly.
images.composition: Three rows, one for each fraction: the fraction and its verdict at the left, a bar or bars of one whole in the middle with a 1 whole bracket above, and for 8/5 the result at the right.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816, three rows. Every whole is a bar exactly 400 px wide and 90 px high with a thin dark #2B2B2B outline (3 px) and thin dark cut lines (2 px). Bar top edges at y 160, 410 and 660. Over the first bar of each row a thin grey #6B7280 bracket line 400 px long (x 330 to x 730, with a 14 px end cap at each end) sits 18 px above the bar, with the text 1 whole centred above it (30 px, dark #1F2937). ROW 1 (8/5): 2 bars side by side, bar 1 at x 330 to 730 cut into exactly 5 equal pieces of 80 px, all 5 filled teal #0072B2, and bar 2 at x 770 to 1170 cut into exactly 5 equal pieces of 80 px, the first 3 filled reddish purple #CC79A7 and the last 2 white; so 8 shaded pieces of 1/5 in all. At the right of bar 2, level with the bars, starting at x 1210, the text = 1 3/5 (bold, 48 px, dark). At the left, centred at x 170, the fraction 8/5 (bold, 64 px, dark, about y 180) and under it the text more than 1 (36 px, about y 240). ROW 2 (3/10): 1 bar at x 330 to 730 cut into exactly 10 equal pieces of 40 px, the first 3 filled teal and the other 7 white; at the left 3/10 (bold, 64 px, about y 430) and under it less than 1 (36 px, about y 490). ROW 3 (10/10): 1 bar at x 330 to 730 cut into exactly 10 equal pieces of 40 px, all 10 filled teal; at the left 10/10 (bold, 64 px, about y 680) and under it equal to 1 (36 px, about y 740). In all 4 bars, 30 pieces, 21 of them shaded (18 teal and 3 purple: row 1 has 5 teal and 3 purple, row 2 has 3 teal, row 3 has 10 teal). Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any whole drawn longer or shorter than the others, or a row with a different number of pieces
purple used anywhere except the 3 pieces of the second bar in row 1
images.takeaway: 8 pieces of 1/5 are more than the 5 that make one whole, 3 pieces of 1/10 are fewer than the 10 that make one whole, and 10 pieces of 1/10 make exactly one whole.
images.description: Three rows of bars of one whole: 8/5 as one full bar and 3 pieces of a second, 3/10 as 3 of 10 pieces, and 10/10 as a full bar of 10 pieces, each with its verdict at the left.
images.context: Concept image for More Than One Whole? Top and Bottom. It follows the idea of the figures in your maths book (pieces of one size counted against the pieces that make one whole) and shows the concept's own three fractions, 8/5, 3/10 and 10/10.
images.teaching_notes: Ask how many pieces make one whole in each row (5, 10, 10), then compare the top number with that count. The slip to watch is saying that a fraction cannot be more than one whole.

image_decisions.why: Pieces counted against one whole of the same length show why the top number against the bottom number decides more than, less than or equal to 1.
